name: Childhood-Onset Epilepsy Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Childhood Epilepsy Criteria

criteria.description: Two or more unprovoked seizures occurring at least 24 hours apart
Seizure onset between 1 and 12 years of age
Characteristic EEG abnormalities consistent with childhood epilepsy syndrome
Exclusion of other neurological or metabolic causes of seizures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent unprovoked seizures with onset between 1 and 12 years and characteristic EEG findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of acute symptomatic seizures and other epilepsy syndromes.

pathognomonic.notes: Typical seizure type in childhood-onset epilepsy syndrome
Brief lapses in awareness characteristic of this syndrome

common.notes: Mild to moderate cognitive impairment in some cases

searchTerms: abnormal brain wave patterns between seizures
seizure-like EEG discharges when not seizing

occasional.notes: Impaired coordination observed in some patients

rare.notes: Includes abnormal heart rate or blood pressure during seizures

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes through serum and CSF analysis
imaging: Normal or nonspecific findings on brain MRI
Occasional hippocampal sclerosis in refractory cases
genetic: Mutations in genes such as SCN1A, GABRG2, and PCDH19 reported in some cases
other: Characteristic EEG patterns including generalized spike-and-wave discharges

distinguishingFeatures: Onset typically in adolescence rather than childhood
Predominance of myoclonic seizures on awakening
Usually occur before age 5 and do not recur without fever

redFlags: Seizure onset before 1 year of age
Refractory seizures unresponsive to standard antiepileptic drugs
references: Fisher RS, et al. ILAE official report: a practical clinical definition of epilepsy. Epilepsia. 2014.
Berg AT, et al. Revised terminology and concepts for organization of seizures and epilepsies: report of the ILAE Commission on Classification and Terminology, 2005-2009. Epilepsia. 2010.
